Header: 2026-04-29 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI, Head of ML), Marcus Bell (SpectrumAI, Platform Eng), Priya Shenoy (SpectrumAI, SRE)
Shared files: pilot-benchmarks.xlsx (link), /shared/redwood-batching-guide.pdf (link)

Summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics. Reviewed last week's benchmarks (tokens per dollar, tokens/sec/$), discussed caching results and batching tradeoffs, flagged higher tail latency in certain QA flows, agreed action items for additional bench runs and a pricing update.

Topics: 1) Cost metrics recap (tokens/sec/$) 2) Prefix/KV caching savings 3) Batching sizes & latency tradeoffs 4) Next steps & pricing

00:00:12 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Hey team, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick 30ish minute sync then QA. Elena, Marcus, Priya, you there?
00:00:20 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Yep, here. Sorry ran a minute late, had an infra ticket.
00:00:28 Jordan Patel (Redwood): No worries. Maya will walk through the numbers first, and then we'll flag the places where cost is highest. Maya?
00:00:36 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Cool, pulling up the sheet — so baseline from last week, unbatched, no cache, was ~1.1 tokens per second per dollar on the gpt-like v2 variant — right now with continuous batching at size 16 and prefix cache on, we're seeing between 3.8 and 4.6 tokens/sec/$ depending on seq length. So roughly a 3.5x improvement in many of your conversational flows. Note: transcription may show the model names wrong, it's the rdlw-13b-q8 variant in our notes.
00:01:12 Marcus Bell (SpectrumAI): That's higher than I expected — are those numbers end-to-end including network egress?
00:01:19 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Good q — these are server-side compute tokens/sec/$, network not included. We can include egress in the next run, but historically egress has been <8% of unit cost for your dataset sizes.
00:01:38 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Marcus, for our throughput peaks the network may matter, Priya correct?
00:01:42 Priya Shenoy (SRE): Yeah we'll want to bench with our VPC peering route, otherwise we see variable tail latencies.
00:01:49 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Noted — Marcus, Priya to run a bench with VPC peering. Add that to action items.
00:01:56 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Quick callout on caching: prefix caching on the assistant prompt saved ~38% token generation in the FAQ flows, but in the summarization job with long context, KV cache gave a 22% savings and reduced GPU time by ~18%. Those are current numbers, variable by template.
00:02:25 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): The 38% looks good — which templates saw the biggest wins?
00:02:30 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Stuff with repeated system prompts and shared context. Your customer-support flow where you prefix a 300-token context saw the biggest wins because the KV cache avoids recomputing attention for the prefix.
00:02:45 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Makes sense.
00:02:50 Marcus Bell (SpectrumAI): There was one run last night where tail latency spiked to 1.2s P99 for short prompts with batch size 32 — any idea why?
00:02:59 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Could be inefficient mixing of very short and long sequences in the same batch — continuous batching can help but you need to set a max-steps-per-batch and sequence bucketing. I recommended a bucket config in the doc we shared but maybe we should tune more aggressively for your distribution.
00:03:18 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Also remember there are tradeoffs: moving to larger batches bumps tokens/sec/$ but can increase P95/P99. For real-time routes we usually cap at batch 8 or 12. For async routes like summarization, batch 32+ works great.
00:03:36 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): For customer-search we need sub-600ms median; we can live with 1.5s P99. For the chat product we need tighter latency.
00:03:46 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Understood — suggestion: split the chat route to a low-latency deployment (dedicated smaller batch, prefer pinned model variant) and a high-throughput route for background tasks. That gives best tokens/sec/$ overall.
00:04:02 Marcus Bell (SpectrumAI): If we split, how much overhead is the second deployment? Is there a minimum committed ratio?
00:04:09 Jordan Patel (Redwood): For pilot we can provision small dedicated capacity without full reserved commit. We'll show estimated monthly delta in the pricing sheet. It won't be huge for your traffic but it depends on peak concurrency.
00:04:22 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Can you show the numbers for that? We need cost per 1M tokens for the two-route split.
00:04:29 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): I have a quick calc: single-route baseline (mixed) ~ $18 per 1M tokens given current pilot config. With split — low-latency route (batch cap 8) accounts for 30% of requests but 50% of cost, so low-latency route cost adds a premium; combined effective cost becomes ~$21-22 per 1M tokens but with improved P99. These are estimated; I'll produce a table.
00:05:02 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Hmm, a 15% cost increase for better latency might be acceptable.
00:05:07 Priya Shenoy (SRE): One note: our retention/legal team asked about data at rest encryption and KMS logs for the pilot — we saw SAML established last week but need to confirm KMS integration for the private route.
00:05:20 Jordan Patel (Redwood): We already shared the security pack in the onboarding folder. For KMS we support customer-managed keys for Private deployments; for Hosted there's envelope encryption. I'll drop the exact KMS doc link after this call.
00:05:33 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Great.
00:05:38 Marcus Bell (SpectrumAI): Back to batching, if Maya sends us the revised batch config, what's the expected delta in tokens/sec/$?
00:05:45 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): If you adopt sequence bucketing + 2-tier batching (immediate small-batch window for short seqs, and delayed larger-batch window for long seqs), we estimate another 20-30% improvement on the flows that currently oscillate. That should push some of your flows up to 5.5-6 tokens/sec/$. But again, P99 tradeoffs need to be measured.
00:06:12 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Excellent. Can you also include guidance on quantization? We ran a q8 model in some tests, but quality checks had occasional hallucinations in multi-step prompts.
00:06:22 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Yeah, quantization helps cost but sometimes increases subtle failure modes. For your multi-step tours, I'd recommend rdlw-13b-q8 for non-critical summarization, but keep rdlw-13b-fp16 for the generation route where precision matters. We can put eval prompts in the harness and run regression checks.
00:06:42 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Action item: Maya to add a small eval set demonstrating quality delta between q8 and fp16 for the top 10 prompt patterns.
00:06:50 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Yep — I'll add that.
00:06:55 Marcus Bell (SpectrumAI): Also curious about cache invalidation — when we update templates, how quickly does prefix cache drop?
00:07:02 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): The prefix cache invalidates on prompt hash change; we also provide TTL controls. For your content where templates change weekly, TTL of 24h is reasonable. If you need faster purge, we can invalidate programmatically via the API.
00:07:19 Priya Shenoy (SRE): For the bench run we're going to enable prefix cache and run a 30-minute steady-state test with our peering — we'll attach logs and pprof traces.
00:07:28 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Perfect. Marcus/Priya file that under CRM-45872.
00:07:34 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): One question on billing: are tokens/sec/$ figures something we can map back to a per-route metering line in billing or it's only aggregate?
00:07:42 Jordan Patel (Redwood): In the Console we provide token-level breakdown by route and model. For pilot we can enable per-route metering exports to your S3 so you can map cost to product features.
00:07:54 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Let's enable that for the next billing cycle.
00:07:58 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Noted.
00:08:02 Maya Chen (Redwood-SE): Last thing — we saw one anomaly where a small subset of prompts (less than 2% volume) had 10x higher compute cost due to long context reconstruction. We'll share a CSV of those examples; I think a template fix or truncation policy will solve it.
00:08:18 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): We'll look.
00:08:22 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Okay let's recap next steps and owners.
00:08:28 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Recap: Maya to send batching & cache config and expected tokens/sec/$ numbers and the q8 vs fp16 eval set. Marcus/Priya to run peered 30-min latency benchmark and upload logs. Jordan to send updated pricing and pilot extension terms and the KMS doc link.
00:08:50 Elena Ruiz (SpectrumAI): Sounds good, thanks everyone.
00:08:55 Jordan Patel (Redwood): We'll target getting those artifacts to you by next Friday (2026-05-01) except the bench which is 2026-05-06.
00:09:03 Marcus Bell (SpectrumAI): Cool. End of my side.
00:09:06 Priya Shenoy (SpectrumAI): Thanks.
00:09:09 Jordan Patel (Redwood): Thanks all — I'll follow up with notes.
